passages.note: House 3rd-reading roll call on SB 101; Clere listed under Nay, not Yea

passages.provision_quote: A governmental entity may substantially burden a person's exercise of religion only if the governmental entity demonstrates that application of the burden to the person: (1) is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest; and (2) is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest.
passages.note: Enrolled Act creates a strict-scrutiny standard for any burden on religious exercise; no clause addresses civil rights or anti-discrimination law one way or the other
Bill-tracking/digest page; lists authors, co-authors and House sponsors, none of whom is Clere; confirms the bill became Public Law on 2015-03-26 but attributes no act or words to Clere

rows.reasoning: Clere voted Nay on SB 101 (2015), a single-subject bill that creates a strict-scrutiny standard barring a governmental entity from substantially burdening religious exercise absent a compelling interest pursued by the least restrictive means, with no clause addressing anti-discrimination law either way. A No vote on this exemption-granting bill shows opposition to that mechanism but does not by itself separate rungs 1-3, which all fall on the side he voted against expanding; excluding rungs 4-5 is not evidence for a specific one of the remaining rungs.
